name: Richard Burr

summary.text: Richard Burr was a Republican US Senator from North Carolina and chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee in early 2020. Senate disclosure records show that he and his wife sold stock worth between roughly $600,000 and $1.7 million in some 30 transactions from late January to February 13, 2020, before the market fell on the COVID-19 pandemic. Burr said he relied solely on public news reports and asked the Senate Ethics Committee to review the sales. The FBI seized his phone in May 2020 and he stepped aside as committee chairman; the Justice Department closed its inquiry without charges in January 2021, and the SEC closed its civil investigation of Burr and his brother-in-law Gerald Fauth with no action in January 2023.

facts.claim: Senate disclosure records show Burr and his wife made at least 30 stock sales between January 31 and February 13, 2020, worth between $600,000 and $1.7 million, with the bulk of the sales on February 13. A closed-door Senate Intelligence Committee briefing on the coronavirus was held on January 24, 2020; Burr's office did not confirm whether he attended.
facts.quote: Senate disclosure records show Burr and his wife made at least 30 stock sales between January 31 and February 13, 2020, worth from $600,000 to $1.7 million.

Report: NC Sen. Burr Sold Up To $1.6M In Stock While Receiving Briefings On Virus

facts.claim: ProPublica reported in March 2020 that Burr sold between $628,000 and $1.72 million of his holdings on February 13, 2020 in 33 separate transactions; later SEC filings put the total at more than $1.6 million.
facts.quote: the precise amount of his stock sales, more than $1.6 million, is also a new detail from this week's SEC filings

facts.claim: On February 7, 2020, Fox News published an op-ed under the names of Senators Lamar Alexander and Richard Burr saying the United States was better prepared than ever before to face emerging public health threats such as the coronavirus.
facts.quote: better prepared than ever before to face emerging public health threats, like the coronavirus

facts.claim: NPR obtained a recording of a February 27, 2020 luncheon at the Capitol Hill Club at which Burr told members of the Tar Heel Circle, a group of North Carolina businesses and organizations, that the virus was much more aggressive in its transmission than anything seen in recent history and probably more akin to the 1918 pandemic.
facts.quote: much more aggressive in its transmission than anything that we have seen in recent history

sources.title: Senator Richard Burr Warned Of Coronavirus Effects In Private Meeting
Senate Intel chair in February privately warned coronavirus was 'akin to 1918 pandemic'

facts.claim: Burr said he relied solely on public news reports, specifically CNBC's reporting from its Asia bureaus, in deciding to sell stock on February 13, 2020, and asked the chairman of the Senate Ethics Committee to open a complete review of the matter.
facts.quote: I relied solely on public news reports to guide my decision regarding the sale of stocks on February 13. Specifically, I closely followed CNBC's daily health and science reporting out of its Asia bureaus at the time.

sources.title: Sen. Burr defends stock sales as fellow Republicans call for investigation

facts.claim: In May 2020 FBI agents seized Burr's Senate-issued cellphone after a search warrant was served on his lawyer; investigators also sought information from his iCloud backup. Burr then stepped aside as chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, saying the step was necessary to allow the committee to continue its work free of external distractions.
facts.quote: I believe this step is necessary to allow the Committee to continue its essential work free of external distractions.

FBI seizes Sen. Richard Burr's cell phone in probe over stock sales

facts.claim: On January 19, 2021, Burr announced that the Department of Justice had informed him it had concluded its review of his personal financial transactions from early 2020 and that the case was closed; no charges were brought.
facts.quote: the Department of Justice informed him that it has concluded its review of his personal financial transactions conducted early last year. The case is now closed.

sources.title: DOJ Drops Insider Trading Investigation Into Sen. Richard Burr
Justice Department closes investigation into Senator Richard Burr over stock sales

facts.claim: The SEC continued a civil investigation after the DOJ closed its case. Court filings made public in October 2021 said the SEC was investigating whether Burr sold stocks on February 13, 2020 on the basis of material nonpublic information, and that Burr's brother-in-law Gerald Fauth called his broker shortly after a phone call with Burr that day. On November 10, 2021 Judge Andrew L. Carter Jr. of the Southern District of New York granted the SEC's application to enforce an investigative subpoena for Fauth's testimony.
facts.quote: SEC staff served Fauth with an investigative subpoena in May 2020 seeking his testimony

sources.title: SEC Obtains Court Order to Enforce Investigative Subpoena for Testimony (Gerald Fauth)
Sen. Richard Burr, brother-in-law spoke on phone just before stock sales that are under investigation, SEC says

facts.claim: On January 6, 2023, Burr announced through his lawyer that the SEC had concluded its investigation into his February 2020 stock trades with no action; Fauth's attorney said the SEC had also closed its investigation into Fauth.
facts.quote: Burr said the SEC informed him that they had concluded their investigation with no action.

SEC closes insider trading probe into former Republican senator

facts.claim: In May 2020 the Justice Department closed its inquiries into the stock trades of Senators Kelly Loeffler, Dianne Feinstein and James Inhofe while continuing to investigate Burr. On June 16, 2020 the Senate Ethics Committee dismissed complaints against Loeffler, its chief counsel writing that the committee did not find evidence that her actions violated federal law, Senate rules or standards of conduct. No separate Senate Ethics Committee action on Feinstein or Inhofe was found.
facts.quote: Based on all the information before it, the Committee did not find evidence that your actions violated federal law, Senate rules, ...

facts.claim: The STOCK Act (Public Law 112-105, enacted April 4, 2012) affirms that Members and employees of Congress are not exempt from the insider-trading prohibitions of the securities laws, including Section 10(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule 10b-5, and requires members to disclose securities transactions within 45 days.
facts.quote: Members and employees of Congress are not exempt from insider trading prohibitions under the securities laws, including section 10(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule 10b-5

connections.quote: Burr said the SEC informed him that they had concluded their investigation with no action.

connections.claim: The Justice Department investigated Burr's early-2020 stock sales, including an FBI seizure of his cellphone under a search warrant in May 2020, and closed the inquiry without charges in January 2021.
connections.quote: the Department of Justice informed him that it has concluded its review of his personal financial transactions conducted early last year. The case is now closed.

openQuestions: The site dates the DOJ closure to May 2020; sources show May 2020 was the FBI phone seizure and the closure of the Loeffler, Feinstein and Inhofe inquiries, while the Burr inquiry closed on January 19, 2021.

The site says the Senate Ethics Committee dismissed complaints against Feinstein and Inhofe; only a Loeffler dismissal (June 16, 2020) was found. CREW's complaint did not name Inhofe because it could not establish he attended the January 24 briefing.
Whether Burr attended the January 24, 2020 briefing was not confirmed by his office in the sources found.
The Senate Ethics Committee's own disposition of Burr's self-requested review was not located.
